quote: The river takes the heavy armor first and the proud men right after.
He counted his gold before counting the archers in the reeds.
source: scribbled on an Alder Bridge milestone

quote: Another banner face-down in peat; the crows won't even bother with the buckle.
Good boots wasted on a corpse that forgot to pause.
They marched out singing and came back as three lines in a ledger.
Even the finest steel turns dull when nobody's left standing to swing it.
The fen doesn't hate you; it simply has room for one more.
He trusted a narrow bridge and an unguarded flank. Both kept their word.
Ashes don't care whether you wore plate or homespun.
source: a chaplain on the Heartland March

quote: A bold charge looks magnificent right up until the crossbows loose.
Keep his ring; leave the body for the tide.
source: a harbor pilot at Burning Harbor

quote: Mercenaries don't mourn—they just divide the rations and check the road.
One sip of healing draught left uncorked in his pack. Shame.
The Ember Court didn't even need to draw swords; hubris did the work.
Here lies a commander who thought formation was just a fancy word.
Fog hides many sins, mostly fatal ones.
When the banner falls, the coin stops flowing, and everyone runs.
He stepped into the caldera expecting a duel and found a furnace.
source: last entry in a charred journal

quote: Not every road leads to a crown; most end in a ditch.
You can't parry a fireball with stubbornness alone.
The crows of Border Fords eat better than kings this season.
He held the line three heartbeats too long.
Even stone wardens crumble; flesh merely does it louder.
Pay the ferryman twice—once going out, once if they drag you back.
Another hero for the ballad-singers to lie about.
Silence settles fast once the last shield drops.
source: a watchman on the Besieged Wall

quote: He forgot that rear-guards are supposed to look behind them.
source: a survivor of the Fleeing Column

quote: Cold iron, cold mud, cold end.
source: chiseled on a Deep Quarry slate

quote: The tide came in right on schedule; the rescue didn't.
source: a fisher on the Iron Coast

quote: Tomorrow another company will march past his bones and swear they're smarter.
A shallow ford only looks safe until the spring melt comes roaring down from the hills.
He spent all his silver on a gilded pommel and nothing on a decent helm.
The reeds never bend for nothing; if there is no wind, draw your blade.
Toll-collectors do not take IOUs, and neither does the river.
source: carved into a post at Alder Ford

quote: Every deserter thinks the woods are kinder than the sergeant, right up until the briar-hounds catch his scent.
Never trust a lantern bobbing where no path has ever been laid.
In the fen, a man's own weight is his worst enemy.
We do not dig graves in Redmarsh; the mud opens its mouth and swallows what falls.
He marched into the bog wearing full plate, sinking like an anvil dropped from a pier.
If the frogs stop croaking all at once, hold your breath and pray your torch doesn't sputter.
Leeches take a drop at a time; the marsh takes everything in a single gulp.
Only fools chase retreating heretics off the boardwalks.
The sea returns what it borrows, usually stripped of meat and tangled in kelp.
A dull blade on the Iron Coast means you forgot your whetstone; a broken blade means you met a barnacle-hulk.
Corsairs count their loot before the blood dries, and the tide washes the ledger clean.
Never turn your back on the surf to admire a shipwreck.
Salt in a wound hurts; salt in the lungs ends the argument.
The cliff-harpies leave the iron behind, so at least the next fool gets a free helmet.
When the ash falls thick enough to muffle footsteps, keep your back to a stone wall.
Men build thrones out of pride and wonder why the foundation turns to cinders.
Fire does not care whether your crest is embroidered in gold or stitched in rags.
He thought heavy steel would save him from the pyre-knights; instead, it cooked him like a chestnut.
The Inquisitor's ink never dries, and his braziers never cool.
All roads to the Cinder Crown end in gray dust.
A merc who refuses to retreat lives half as long as a coward and dies twice as poor.
Check your bowstring before rain, and check your flank before glory.
Magic burns bright until the caster runs out of breath—or blood.
Raising the dead is easy; convincing them not to drag you down with them is the trick.
Steel blunts, shields splinter, and heroes rot just like farmers.
He died with three healing draughts still corked in his belt.
Courage without caution is just a faster way to feed the crows.
The river remembers every debt, even when the ledger sinks.
source: an old fisherman at Alder Bridge

quote: Never drink water that shines green under moonlight.
A knight in Redmarsh is just a slower meal for the rot-hounds.
Rust eats royal iron just as hungrily as peasant tin.
If you hear chanting over the surf, plug your ears and run for high ground.
Ashes make poor mortar for an empire.
He challenged the executioner without checking the weight of his own shield.
Even the sharpest sword cannot parry a blow you refused to see coming.
Gold weighs nothing in a dead man's purse.
The border was drawn in ink, held in iron, and paid for in orphans.
Step light on the moss; beneath it waits ten feet of cold black hunger.
We burn our dead so they stay dead. Pity no one was left to burn him.
A galley oar breaks the back; a corsair's hook finishes the rest.
The sea cliff has no mercy for clumsy boots.
Smoke blinds the eyes long before flame touches the skin.
The Crown promised glory; all it delivered was charcoal.
A good mercenary knows when to advance; a rich one knows when to run.
Wolves hunt in packs, yet men still insist on wandering the fens alone.
No charm wards off plain stupidity.
His shield was stout, his sword was keen, and his positioning was fatal.
Blood washes off stone easily; it never quite leaves the mud.
Tides wait for no king, and certainly not for a bleeding sellsword.
When the brazier flares white, step back or become kindling.
Another name crossed off the bounty board, another mug poured in silence.
The marsh keeps its secrets well—mostly because nobody comes back to tell them.
Salt preserves meat, yet it rots everything else on this wretched coast.
Even embers cool when there is nothing left to burn.
He counted his kills instead of watching his stamina.
Here lies another hero who forgot that numbers win wars, not pride.
